title: Two-regime IR/UV mixed spectral-counting envelope for the normalized Green trace
question: Can low and high spectral modes be controlled by different sublinear counting exponents, avoiding an unjustified single common alpha while retaining a finite trace envelope?

new_perspective.principle: For a split 1<=r<m and exponents 0<alpha_IR,alpha_UV<1, use C_IR=max_(k<=r) k/lambda_k^alpha_IR and C_UV=max_(k>r) k/lambda_k^alpha_UV. Bound the head by C_IR^(1/alpha_IR) sum_(k<=r) k^(-1/alpha_IR) and the tail by C_UV^(1/alpha_UV) sum_(k>r) k^(-1/alpha_UV), with an integral tail beyond m.
route: Enumerate every declared exponent pair and every admissible split on every actual likelihood row.
Keep IR and UV constants and finite sums separate; compare only the UV tail with its explicit integral remainder.
Select the smallest mixed envelope only as a diagnostic; do not promote row-wise selections to a common alpha or common split.
Reject alpha>=1, unsorted spectra, exponent-power inversion, split-index mistakes, Fiedler-only shortcuts and disconnected graphs in the hostile lane.
Promote only if one pair and a controlled split rule remain uniformly bounded on a common Hamiltonian core and transfer through the R-399 shell.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: A two-regime envelope matches the expected separation of infrared physical modes and ultraviolet regulator modes. It can only support the physical route after a uniform split rule, common-core control, R-399 shell transfer and the remaining OS/KMS/GNS and Sector-A reconstruction are proved.

finite_theorem.scope: The implication is finite-dimensional; neither exponent pair, split nor constant is asserted uniform in cutoff, volume, phase or exhaustion.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks only scalar exponent and split-tail positivity plus a finite numerical instance; ordered matrix spectra, Gibbs rows and all uniform or physical limits remain in the executable/open boundary.

promotion_criteria: Prove a fixed or analytically controlled split rule and positive uniform lower bounds for the IR and UV counting constants on one Hamiltonian common core.
Control the pair and split under cutoff, volume, phase, source and exhaustion changes.
Transfer the mixed trace envelope to the R-399 conditional shell and combine it with the R-406 Schur residual split before any common-alpha or GNS promotion.
stop_conditions: If every tested pair or split develops an unbounded constant under validated stress, retain the finite mixed comparison and register the obstruction instead of claiming uniform control.
If either exponent is >=1, the corresponding zeta tail is divergent and the route must stop; if ordering, powers or split membership are mishandled, record the exact failed inequality.
Finite mixed counting and tail positivity are not a uniform, phase-selection, common-core, GNS, physical-gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A theorem.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite mixed IR/UV spectral-counting and zeta-tail checkpoint only. It proves no cutoff-, volume-, source-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform bound, common core, common split rule, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: Allowing separate IR and UV exponents avoids imposing a single finite exponent, but it does not establish a regulator-independent split or constants.
